a02_bindless_atomic_first_hole.rule_note: bindless atomic_fetch_add at index=8 (first_hole), then a SECOND dispatch (canary readback) that reuses the same OUT buffer -- out[] in the frozen record is the K=8 canary texture_buffer readback ONLY; the atomic's own previous-value output from the first dispatch is overwritten by the second dispatch's writes to the same buffer offsets (a known design limitation, not a claim about the atomic's return value; the readback still validly answers 'did the OOB/hole atomic corrupt a real entry')

a02_bindless_atomic_first_oob.rule_note: bindless atomic_fetch_add at index=256 (first_oob), then a SECOND dispatch (canary readback) that reuses the same OUT buffer -- out[] in the frozen record is the K=8 canary texture_buffer readback ONLY; the atomic's own previous-value output from the first dispatch is overwritten by the second dispatch's writes to the same buffer offsets (a known design limitation, not a claim about the atomic's return value; the readback still validly answers 'did the OOB/hole atomic corrupt a real entry')

a02_bindless_atomic_first_populated.rule_note: bindless atomic_fetch_add at index=0 (first_populated), then a SECOND dispatch (canary readback) that reuses the same OUT buffer -- out[] in the frozen record is the K=8 canary texture_buffer readback ONLY; the atomic's own previous-value output from the first dispatch is overwritten by the second dispatch's writes to the same buffer offsets (a known design limitation, not a claim about the atomic's return value; the readback still validly answers 'did the OOB/hole atomic corrupt a real entry')

a02_bindless_atomic_mirror_probe.rule_note: bindless atomic_fetch_add at index=512 (mirror_probe), then a SECOND dispatch (canary readback) that reuses the same OUT buffer -- out[] in the frozen record is the K=8 canary texture_buffer readback ONLY; the atomic's own previous-value output from the first dispatch is overwritten by the second dispatch's writes to the same buffer offsets (a known design limitation, not a claim about the atomic's return value; the readback still validly answers 'did the OOB/hole atomic corrupt a real entry')

a02_bindless_read_first_hole.rule_note: bindless read at index=8: first in-array, never-encoded hole (index K, < CAP); hypothesis: 0 (guard-fill 0xDE...DE does not decode to a valid resource)

a02_bindless_read_first_oob.rule_note: bindless read at index=256: first index beyond the declared array bound (index == CAP); C++-style array OOB, real hardware behavior under test

a02_bindless_read_first_populated.rule_note: bindless read at index=0: first populated (canary 0)

a02_bindless_read_last_hole.rule_note: bindless read at index=255: last in-array hole (index CAP-1)

a02_bindless_read_last_populated.rule_note: bindless read at index=7: last populated canary (index K-1)

a02_bindless_read_mirror_probe.rule_note: bindless read at index=512: OOB at exactly 2*CAP -- mirroring probe in the EXP-0083 tradition (that experiment found the buffer base-slot selector mirrors at a power-of-two period); hypothesis: either 0 (no mirroring) or equals index-0's content (period-CAP mirroring)

a02_bindless_read_oob_2x_minus1.rule_note: bindless read at index=511: OOB stress point just below 2*CAP

a02_direct_atomic_boundary.rule_note: the read_write (atomic) ceiling is 8, not 128 (pre-freeze exploration: MSL rejects a 9th access::read_write texture argument at compile time). atomic_fetch_add(+1) at the last legal read_write slot (index 7, texture_buffer<uint> -- fixed from an earlier draft that mismatched the kernel's declared texture_buffer argument type with a plain texture2d resource); out[0] = the value atomic_fetch_add returns (the PRE-add value, 7, since slot i was CPU-populated with content i)

a02_direct_atomic_illegal.rule_note: atomic_fetch_add with idx=8: no compile-time branch matches any of the 8 declared read_write slots (there is no 9th slot to select -- this is the direct path's structural ceiling, not a runtime OOB read); kernel's own not-matched sentinel expected

a02_direct_read_boundary.rule_note: 128 direct [[texture(N)]] read-access slots (the exact ceiling from pre-freeze exploration), read at index 0/63/127 (exact) and idx=UINT32_MAX (no compile-time branch matches, kernel's own 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel expected -- NOT a hardware runtime-selector overflow, since the direct index is chosen at COMPILE time, not runtime; see RESULTS for this distinction from EXP-0083's runtime byte-splice census)

a02_direct_write_and_readback.rule_note: 128 direct write-access slots (access::write is NOT subject to the 8-slot read_write ceiling, per pre-freeze exploration), write at index 5, readback first 8 canaries -- only index 5 should change
